title: Kase - August 2026
byline: An operations management system I have been building. Here is what it does.
content:
Kase is an operations management system. Work comes in, a set of things have to happen in order before that work is done, and Kase is what runs those things and tells you where everything is sitting. Here is what it does today.

PIPELINES
The order of the steps is configuration, not code. You define a pipeline for a kind of work - send this email, wait for an approval, assign it to someone, hit this webhook - and Kase walks it one step at a time.

Change the flow and nobody ships a deploy. That is the whole reason it exists.

EVERYTHING RUNS ON A QUEUE
Steps run async. Work gets created, the first step goes on the queue, something picks it up, runs it, and queues the next one. Nothing sits there blocking the person who raised it.

APPROVALS AND HOLDS
An approval step parks the work and the pipeline stops. It stays parked for as long as it needs to, and picks up exactly where it left off the moment a person approves.

No cron job polling a table every minute asking whether a human did the thing yet.

SIX KINDS OF STEP
  • Send a communication
  • Assign an agent
  • Call a webhook
  • Ask for an approval
  • Hold
  • Kick off more work

Step types are plugins, so a seventh one is a new file and nothing else. If two of them ever claim the same name the app refuses to start rather than quietly picking one.

ACCESS
Every request gets its token checked on the way in. Roles decide what you can touch, and permissions are looked up fresh each time - pull someone out of a role and it applies RIGHT NOW, not whenever their session felt like expiring.

UNDER IT
Java, Spring Boot, Postgres, Kafka. Schema changes are versioned files and the app is not allowed to edit the database on its own, so if the code and the database disagree it refuses to start.

It lives at kase.avirana.com.
